entries.title: Gajakesari Yoga
entries.body: Learning, good judgement and support from others are the traditional themes of this pattern. A practical way to explore it is to ask for advice, then explain your own reasoning before making a decision. It does not mean that you are automatically wise, famous or protected from difficulty.

entries.title: Budha-Aditya Yoga
entries.body: This pattern offers a way to think about expressing ideas clearly. The cited historical passage connects the Sun and Mercury together with skill at work and recognition. Astrisk treats those as symbolic themes, not promises of intelligence or fame. In everyday life, you could practise explaining one idea in a few sentences, ask someone what they understood, and improve the explanation. In a relationship, being persuasive is different from listening: leave room for a partner to disagree without needing to win. Mercury often stays near the Sun, so this combination alone is not exceptional. Other computed chart conditions supply context, but none measures your actual ability. Reflection: where would clearer communication make your week easier?

entries.title: Chandra-Mangala Yoga
entries.body: The useful reflection here is how feelings become action. The historical passage joins the Moon and Mars and discusses practical enterprise, but also makes moral and family judgments that Astrisk does not adopt. A modern discussion can focus on choosing a constructive response when something matters to you. For example, turn an exciting idea into a small trial before spending heavily or making a commitment. In relationships, explain what you need and check the other person's understanding rather than assuming they share your urgency. The chart cannot tell whether you are angry, entrepreneurial or in conflict with a parent. Reflection: what helps you pause long enough to choose a response you will still agree with tomorrow?

entries.title: Ruchaka Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Taking initiative, setting boundaries and following through are the traditional themes here. Choose a realistic challenge and work on it steadily, with space for feedback and rest. This pattern does not choose your career or measure physical ability.

entries.title: Bhadra Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Clear communication, curiosity and practical problem-solving are the themes associated with this pattern. Try breaking a complicated task into steps or checking that another person understood what you meant. Learning depends on opportunity and practice, not a chart label.

entries.title: Hamsa Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: This pattern is traditionally associated with learning, guidance and a sense of purpose. Consider what you would like to learn, who can teach you and where your own experience might help someone else. It does not make a person morally superior or guarantee good fortune.

entries.title: Malavya Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Appreciation, creativity and balanced relationships are the traditional themes. Make time for a creative interest or talk openly about what makes a shared space comfortable for both people. A chart cannot promise an attractive partner, a happy marriage or material comforts.

entries.title: Sasa Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Patience, responsibility and building something that lasts are the themes of this pattern. A manageable routine, clear boundaries and shared responsibilities can be useful things to reflect on. You do not need to accept hardship to fulfil a chart; support and rest matter too.

entries.title: Raja Yoga (kendra-trikona)
entries.body: This pattern traditionally connects personal initiative with purpose and responsibility. Reflect on a skill you would like to develop and one way to use it in work or community life. Despite its royal name, it does not promise leadership, status or success.

entries.title: Dhana Yoga
entries.body: This pattern is traditionally discussed in relation to resources, learning and opportunities. Use it as a prompt to review practical goals and the skills or support needed to pursue them. It is not a financial forecast or a reason to make an investment; seek qualified advice for financial decisions.

entries.title: Vipreet Raja Yoga
entries.body: The traditional theme is finding constructive responses to difficult circumstances. Think about a challenge you can address, the support available and one small step within your control. It does not predict a crisis or mean that suffering is necessary for success.

entries.title: Adhi Yoga
entries.body: This pattern is traditionally discussed through support and responsibility. The historical passage uses royal and military roles to express influence. Those roles are not a career prediction; a useful present-day reflection is how you seek advice and handle responsibilities that affect other people. Before a difficult decision, identify what you know, what remains uncertain and whose experience could help. In a partnership, clarify what support each person can realistically offer instead of assuming one must always be strong. The pattern does not guarantee protection, health, wealth or authority. Reflection: what decision would benefit from a calmer conversation and a second perspective?

entries.title: Sunapha Yoga
entries.body: Developing resources through your own effort is the useful theme in this traditional pattern. The cited passage praises self-acquired resources and reputation. Astrisk does not turn that praise into a forecast of money or status. Resources can also mean a skill, dependable routines or people you can ask for help. For example, choose one skill you genuinely want to improve, set a modest practice schedule and judge progress from what you learn. In a relationship, discuss how to share responsibilities without equating earning power with personal worth. A chart does not measure intelligence or independence. Reflection: what small investment of time would give you more useful options?

entries.title: Anapha Yoga
entries.body: This pattern can be explored through self-direction and the space to make considered choices. The historical description praises composure and influence, while also making guarantees about health and sorrow that are not reliable personal conclusions. A practical reflection is whether your routine gives you enough quiet time to decide what matters. You might reserve a short break before replying to a difficult message or say clearly when you need time to think. In relationships, solitude and closeness need to be negotiated rather than assumed. This pattern does not prove confidence, wellbeing or freedom from difficulty. Reflection: which boundary would help you be more present when you return to other people?

entries.title: Durudhara Yoga
entries.body: Giving and receiving practical support is a useful way to discuss this pattern. Its historical description speaks of comforts, resources and generosity through the social arrangements of its time. A present-day reflection might be how you share work, ask for help and make room for rest. Try naming a responsibility that could be shared and agreeing on what help would actually look like. In a relationship, support is mutual and freely chosen; neither person should be treated as the other's servant. The chart cannot establish whether you have money, help or a supportive family. Reflection: where are you taking on too much, or overlooking an opportunity to contribute?

entries.title: Kemadruma Yoga
entries.body: Treat this label with particular care. The old text contains harsh social and moral judgments, but it also records exceptions and competing conditions. Astrisk rejects those judgments: a chart pattern does not establish poverty, loneliness, wrongdoing or illness. The only useful reflective direction here is to notice what helps you feel connected and supported. You might choose a reliable routine, contact someone you trust or ask for practical help when needed. These are ordinary options, not remedies required by your chart. Different schools apply different cancellation rules; the application only reports its selected engine rule. Do not reject a partner, spend money on a cure or tolerate mistreatment because of this label. Reflection: which source of support feels safe and available to you now?

entries.title: Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga
entries.body: This pattern describes a chart condition that offsets another condition traditionally called challenging. In everyday terms, it is a reminder that one label never tells the whole story and that support can change how challenges are approached. It does not prove past hardship or promise future success. The technical cancellation is computed by the engine, not inferred from your life.

entries.title: Kala Sarpa (pattern)
entries.body: This is a geometric grouping of planets on one side of the Moon's nodal axis, interpreted differently across traditions. If you choose to use it symbolically, consider balance between the areas of life that receive most of your attention. It is not a curse or a reason to buy remedies. This later interpretive pattern should never outweigh the rest of the chart or your own experience.
